articles.title: Linkdaze’s smart calendar is built to run a household, not just track a schedule | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Linkdaze's smart digital calendar stands out for not putting its features behind a paywall, including an AI meal planner tool.
articles.body:
With back-to-school season approaching (or already here in some places), keeping track of everyone’s schedules can get pretty chaotic. Between work, school, appointments, sports, chores, and everything else going on, a regular paper calendar just doesn’t cut it. That’s where Linkdaze’s smart digital calendar comes in — a touchscreen tablet built specifically to organize a household rather than a single person.

One of Linkdaze’s biggest strengths is its calendar compatibility. The system can synchronize calendars from popular services, including Google, iCloud, Outlook, Yahoo, and Cozi, which is a dedicated family-organizing app. This is particularly useful for families where different members use different platforms. Instead of asking everyone to switch to a single calendar app, Linkdaze brings multiple schedules together and uses color coding to make individual family members easy to identify.

Launched last December, Linkdaze is available in 15.6-inch and 10.1-inch models, giving you some flexibility depending on how much wall space you have. Beyond calendars and appointments, you can use it for chores and rewards, meal planning, shopping lists, and other family organization. It can even double as a digital photo frame for displaying family photos.

The most interesting feature, however, is Linkdaze’s AI meal planner with “Snap-to-Sync.” Instead of manually entering everything into a meal-planning app, you can take a photo of a paper recipe or your kid’s school lunch menu. Linkdaze will turn that information into a digital meal plan and generate a shopping list from it. While not an entirely new idea, it’s a useful feature that helps Linkdaze stand out from a basic digital calendar.

Another big plus is that Linkdaze doesn’t require a monthly subscription for its main features. It’s an interesting choice in a category where recurring revenue has become the default. Skylight, a competing smart-calendar brand, offers additional features through its $79 per year subscription. For a hardware company entering a crowded smart-display market, that decision is either going to differentiate its product or look like a lost revenue stream.

Linkdaze is also less expensive up front, with the 10.1-inch model priced at $119.99 (currently discounted to $66 on Amazon ) compared with Skylight’s 10-inch model starting at $149.99 (if you pay for the subscription.)

Overall, this device could make a practical gift for busy parents who are trying to keep everyone’s schedules in one place. It could also be a great fit for college apartments, where roommates can use it to coordinate chores, study schedules, shared meals, and other household responsibilities. It’s also very helpful for those of us juggling interviews, deadlines, meetings, and story assignments.

This post was first published on August 20, 2026.

articles.title: New TV shows to watch this week: Tune in to ‘Lanterns’ on HBO, stream ‘My Brilliant Career’ on Netflix and revisit ‘Heroes’ on Tubi
articles.summary: Kyle Chandler and Aaron Pierre sink their teeth into a superhero adaptation, while Netflix releases a delightful Australian period romance.
articles.body:
Hey TV watchers! TV critic Michel Ghanem here. Every two weeks, I highlight the shows worth your TV time for Trust Me, I Watch Everything . Whether you prefer sticking to cable, catching the latest on streaming or digging up a hidden gem that slipped through the cracks, I try to curate something for everyone.

Can you believe summer is coming to a close? A few late August series have arrived to keep us entertained before the fall TV season is upon us. This week, consider tuning in to Adults, a low-stakes hangout comedy airing on FXX, or the HBO superhero adaptation Lanterns . Over on streaming, Netflix's My Brilliant Career is for those who love a period drama with a love triangle. Finally, in light of Hayden Panettiere's tragic death at 36, consider revisiting her breakout role in Heroes on Netflix or Tubi. Plus, a few other recommendations below.

Why you should watch it: Debatably, the Green Lanterns of the DC Comics aren't the flashiest superheroes. They are not mutants with superhuman abilities. Rather, the Lanterns are ordinary humans and aliens alike who wield superpowered rings provided by an intergalactic enforcement agency that help them fly, create force fields and project various green objects. Basically, they're the universe's police force — with rings they need to charge periodically, lest they find themselves completely ordinary without them.

Luckily, Lanterns is in good hands. The eight-episode drama is created by Chris Mundy ( Ozark ), Damon Lindelof ( Watchmen ) and comic book writer Tom King. Kyle Chandler stars as Hal Jordan, a former pilot and member of the Green Lantern Corps responsible for keeping Earth safe from extraterrestrial threats. He's also been training his recruit, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), for many years.

The two men get caught up in an incident in the small town of Rushville, Neb., where Hal quickly butts heads with local sheriff Kerry Kane (Kelly Macdonald) over how to handle a suspicious shooting. It all spirals into something much bigger, with a cast that also features Garret Dillahunt, Poorna Jagannathan, Jason Ritter and Nathan Fillion (reprising his hilariously grating Justice Gang member Guy Gardner from Superman ).

I wouldn't watch expecting the show to immediately jump into bright-green action sequences like an animated Justice League episode ; there's definitely more intrigue and story-building in these early episodes as we find out more about what's actually happening. Lindelof's Watchmen came out swinging from the jump, but this show has more of a True Detective slow burn.

In the spectrum of superhero adaptations on television, Lanterns is a very decent and engaging offering. It's accessible enough that you don't need to have watched anything else in the DC extended universe to jump in, and there's enough sci-fi suspense to keep you anticipating the next episode.

How to watch: New episodes of Lanterns stream every Sunday at 9 p.m. ET on HBO Max and air simultaneously on HBO.

Why you should watch it: Will there ever be another Friends ? Sitcoms about tight-knit friend groups who may or may not date each other are in rare supply these days. Adults , created by The Tonight Show comedy writing duo Ben Kronengold and Rebecca Shaw, might just be filling that gap.

We follow a group of post-college 20-somethings who all live together in their friend Samir's (Malik Elassal) house. The group in question includes Billie (Lucy Freyer), a stress-prone journalism major working in media; Anton (Owen Thiele), a remote worker with the special ability to befriend pretty much anyone; and Issa (Amita Rao), who is working overtime to get the household to accept her Canadian boyfriend, Paul Baker (Jack Innanen), into their crew.

It's all funny misadventures and dinner parties gone wrong, but half the fun is the scenes packed with bits and witty dialogue. I can't yet divulge anything juicy from the second season, which premieres on Aug. 27, but I can confirm there are some exciting guest stars (like Zosia Mamet, Raven-Symoné, Gaten Matarazzo) and a very queer love triangle set up in the first season's finale. Take this as your sign to catch up before it returns.

Adults is an easy recommendation in a television landscape with bloated episodes and an over-reliance on murder mysteries. The stakes are low in comparison, and episodes clock in at around 25 minutes, are tightly structured and move quickly. Before you know it, you'll feel right at home with your new group of friends.

How to watch: The new season of Adults premieres on Thursday, Aug. 27 at 9 p.m. ET on FXX with two episodes. Episodes will stream simultaneously on Hulu .

Why you should watch it: If you loved The Other Bennet Sister , Little Women and/or Bridgerton , you should make your way expeditiously to watch Netflix's new Australian period drama, My Brilliant Career , created by Liz Doran.

Based on the 1901 novel of the same name by Miles Franklin (and previously adapted as a film in 1979), the series stars Philippa Northeast as Sybylla Melvyn, a sassy aspiring writer stuck in the rural town of Possum Gully. She's encouraged by her family to move to Caddagat with the hopes of both furthering her writing career and finding a husband along the way. (Sybylla has little to no interest in centering a search for a partner, but since her family's financial future depends on it, the pressure is on.)

Life in Caddagat with her wealthy grandmother, Winifred (Anna Chancellor), and her widowed aunt, Helen (Genevieve O'Reilly), is a little different. There are rules of early 1900s society in place here; decorum and expectations of dress must be considered. But Sybylla has little regard for these aspects of higher society. She just wants to write her modern poetry in peace — and snort while she laughs without someone pointing it out.

Things take a turn when she meets two potential suitors: Harry Beecham (Christopher Chung), a very muscular Chinese Australian, and Frank Hawden (Jake Dunn), an English foreman. This is when the story leans more toward a typical love triangle affair as Sybylla finds herself unexpectedly yearning for romance, but it's all enjoyable enough to watch.

The series moves quickly across six episodes and is energetic, using an anachronistic soundtrack and some nice-looking cinematography that elevate it beyond the usual Netflix fare. Sybylla is easy to root for, even at her most chaotic. My Brilliant Career is a very strong entry in the romance-period-drama genre for those willing to take the plunge.

How to watch: All six episodes of My Brilliant Career are streaming on Netflix.

Outer Banks: The compelling teen drama set in North Carolina first premiered in 2020, and now returns for its fifth and final season . It remains one of Netflix's most popular series, and some of the cast — Drew Starkey in particular — have broken out to broader career success. See what's in store for one final adventure with the Pogues. — Now streaming on Netflix .

Why you should watch it: In light of Hayden Panettiere's untimely death , you may want to revisit her breakout role as Claire Bennet in NBC's iconic superhero drama, Heroes .

The landscape of superhero television has changed drastically since 2006. Marvel hadn't yet found the foothold it now has, and it was bold to debut an original series that bore a vague resemblance to X-Men without the foundation of comic books or previous films. Having recently rewatched the first season, I can confirm the series still holds up and should be held up as an example of how to make a propulsive, character-driven series that balances an overall plot with smaller, disparate arcs.

The show had a large ensemble cast, with high schooler Claire (Panettiere) playing a pivotal role when a prophecy sets Peter Petrelli (Milo Ventimiglia) on a mission to "save the cheerleader, save the world." The other heroes in question include Hiro Nakamura (Masi Oka), who has the ability to teleport and manipulate time; Nathan Petrelli (Adrian Pasdar), Peter's brother, who can fly; Matt Parkman (Greg Grunberg), a police officer and mind-reader; and Niki Sanders (Ali Larter), who finds out she has a split personality with a much stronger, brazen version of herself.

Each character gets a piece of the story as they discover their abilities, but become connected when the story's villain, Sylar (Zachary Quinto), begins eliminating the superpowered one by one in the most horrific way possible — sawing open their heads and consuming their brains, absorbing their abilities in the process.

There's also an organization hunting the heroes down, and a scientist studying how human DNA evolved to include these abilities in the first place.

Before going more off the rails in later seasons (and in a later spin-off, Heroes: Reborn , that couldn't quite recapture the magic), Heroes was a masterclass in complex storytelling. It's hard to imagine a broadcast network show quite as ambitious — or a version of this show that would have worked without Panettiere's performance.

How to watch: All four seasons of Heroes are available to stream on Netflix or for free with ads on Tubi .

That's the end of this week's episode, but there'll always be more TV to watch. I'll be back on Sept. 7 with new recommendations.

Think there's something missing that deserves my TV time? Let me know what else I should have on my radar in the comments below!

articles.title: De-Googled GrapheneOS is coming to Motorola’s foldables next year
articles.summary: ﻿The open source take on Android is also planning Pixel 11 support soon.
articles.body: GrapheneOS, an open source version of Android that prioritizes security and privacy, has detailed its plans for supporting Motorola smartphones. Official support is set to arrive next year, starting with traditional flagships, before rolling out to Motorola’s foldable phones and perhaps cheaper models, eventually.  In a Mastodon thread, the GrapheneOS Foundation announced that it will initially support a Motorola slab flagship phone, but will later support both Razr Fold and Razr Ultra foldables — the latter of which would be the first flip phone to officially run GrapheneOS. Graphene has always had stringent security standards when it comes to hardware. The organization said that this year’s Motorola Signature and Razr handsets are “very close to meeting our requirements,” but lack mature support for hardware memory tagging and secure element integration. The organization expects the next generation of Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite chips to meet its standards, which is why it’s targeting Motorola’s 2027 phones for initial support. Earlier this month Graphene confirmed that its initial Motorola devices would be flagships that would “be higher end hardware than Pixels at a higher price.” More affordable devices are on the roadmap, but would require better security features from Qualcomm for its cheaper chips, and for Motorola to invest in seven years of software support for those phones — this year’s $499.99 Moto G Stylus only promised two major OS upgrades and three years of security updates. Motorola first announced its collaboration with Graphene in March, saying that the two organizations would “work to strengthen smartphone security.” Until now, Graphene has only officially supported Google’s Pixel phones. That support is ongoing, and the organization confirmed it has plans to add support for the Pixel 11 series in the future. However, it noted that changes to the Android Open Source Project’s support for Pixel phones mean they are now “harder to properly support than many other devices.” In contrast, it said “Motorola is doing a large portion of the work of porting GrapheneOS to their devices.”

articles.title: 'Yellowstone' creator Taylor Sheridan sued by writer alleging he stole her idea
articles.summary: The hit drama, which ran for six years, is now the subject of a copyright lawsuit.
articles.body:
A writer is suing Yellowstone creator Taylor Sheridan, alleging he stole the idea for the show from a project she'd spent more than 10 years developing.

Lauren J. Salkin alleges that the hit drama series bears striking similarities to a script she pitched to Sheridan's team in 2016 and 2017, sharing "specific expressive choices," according to the lawsuit filed Friday and reviewed by TheWrap , Variety and the Independent . The suit also names 101 Studios, Paramount Global, NBCUniversal and other companies behind the show as defendants.

Yahoo News has reached out to Sheridan's representatives for comment.

Salkin says she submitted a completed pilot script for her own show, Sovereign Nation , along with a series bible and pitch deck, to Sheridan's representatives at Elevate Entertainment. The complaint describes Sovereign Nation as a "dramatic television series centered on tribal governance, casino-driven economic power and a modern war over land and development."

Yellowstone follows the Dutton family, owners of the largest ranch in Montana, as they navigate conflicts over land with developers, a neighboring Native American reservation and other parties.

Yellowstone ran for six years, from 2018 to 2024, becoming a massive hit for Paramount Network. Its star, Kevin Costner, won a Golden Globe for his role. The show has spawned four spinoffs; its latest, Dutton Ranch , was released in May. Three more spinoffs are in development.

Salkin's suit states that Sheridan's representatives told her he "thanks you very much for your interest," but "unfortunately, he's unavailable for TV projects," and that Paramount greenlighted Yellowstone just months later.

Salkin also says she met with a senior HBO executive who had reviewed her Sovereign Nation pitch. According to TheWrap 's account of the lawsuit, Salkin says the executive later told her HBO had rejected a Sheridan pitch for Yellowstone in spring 2017 because of its similarities to her work.

According to Variety , the suit states: "When the works are objectively compared, the same coordinated design repeatedly appears: casino-centered institutions organize political power; the same unusual land-development mechanisms propel the conflict; parallel scenes perform the same dramatic functions; and the same actors appear in materially parallel roles.

"These are not merely convergences of a shared genre. Taken together with access and timing, they support a strong inference of copying."

Speaking to Yahoo News, Salkin's attorney Paul B. Lackey said: "Obviously, it was not an easy decision for an individual screenwriter to decide to take on the titans of the entertainment industry.

"She has watched the exploitation of her hard work for too long and decided that enough was enough. We will now hold them accountable."

Salkin's lawyers also claim she suggested actors Danny Huston and Gil Birmingham, who appeared in Yellowstone , in her pitch deck.

Sheridan had worked with Birmingham on two films: Hell or High Water (2016) and Wind River , which was filmed in March and April 2016, several months before Salkin submitted her pitch to Elevate in late 2016 and early 2017.

Salkin is seeking an injunction against the continued use of her work, along with unspecified damages and profits tied to the alleged infringement. She has also requested a jury trial, according to HollywoodLife .

Sheridan has previously given his own account of the origins of Yellowstone . In 2023, he told the Hollywood Reporter that he pitched the project to HBO as a movie — The Godfather in Montana — before it evolved into the series that aired on Paramount Network.

articles.title: Mariska Hargitay's friends warned her not to host the Emmys. Then she decided it was worth the risk.
articles.summary: The "Law & Order: SVU" star explains why she ignored her friends' advice and took the gig — and how former "Colbert" writers are helping.
articles.body:
Mariska Hargitay is having an epic year.

The actor made her Broadway debut in the one-woman show Every Brilliant Thing this spring. Then in the summer, her beloved New York Knicks won their first NBA title in more than 50 years — she was courtside for their miraculous 29-point comeback in Game 4 of the NBA Finals. This fall, she's returning for her 28th (!) season of Law & Order: Special Victims Unit .

That's not all: In a few weeks, she'll host the Emmy Awards, becoming the first woman to do so in 15 years. My Mom Jayne , the HBO documentary she directed about her mother, Jayne Mansfield, is nominated for three awards.

When NBC and the Television Academy announced that she would host the Emmys, Hargitay said in a statement that it was a " great honor " for her to "celebrate this extraordinary community of storytellers."

But in a recent interview with Variety , Hargitay said that when NBC asked, she almost said no.

"At first I thought, 'This is ridiculously thankless — a difficult job that everyone gets ripped apart for. Why? Why would I do that?'" Hargitay recalled.

She said she then consulted with friends who had hosted awards shows, and they all told her the same thing: "Don't do it."

But her love for the medium, combined with a desire for new challenges, led her to go for it.

"I thought about why I love television," Hargitay said. "Television, in my opinion, is extraordinarily healing."

She's working with ex-'Late Show' writers

While Hargitay is the first non-comedian to host the Emmys since Angela Lansbury in 1993, she'll have some help.

In a recent interview with Deadline , Hargitay said that she's enlisted some of the writers from The Late Show With Stephen Colbert , which ended earlier this year, to help write her Emmys material.

"We're at the beginning stages, and so we're throwing out a lot of different ideas," she said. "I'm working with an incredible team of writers — the writers from Colbert … We've been meeting a lot and discussing a lot and pitching a lot of ideas. We're pitching so many ideas."

"I cannot tell you how many people — famous people — ask to be a dead body on the show. It's a thing," Hargitay said. "And it is so funny to me that that's what they want out of all the things … just to be a dead body. It's on their bucket list. That's one of the ideas that we were talking about."

Like several other New York-based stars , Hargitay is a diehard Knicks fan and has been a courtside fixture at their Madison Square Garden home games for years.

"And I'm a Knick!" she exclaimed at one point during her Variety interview.

She has become friends with point guard Jalen Brunson, who calls her "my favorite New York Knicks fan."

"I'm so grateful for the relationship we have been able to build over the last few years," Brunson told Variety. "As a lifelong fan of 'SVU,' her support means the world to me. I'm truly grateful to have her in my corner."

Brunson also attended the New York premiere of My Mom Jayne and a performance of Every Brilliant Thing , the Broadway show that Hargitay starred in during the Knicks' championship run.

Hargitay told Variety that she half-jokingly asked to have the night off to watch the Knicks' title-clinching Game 5, which was played in San Antonio. She said she watched the second half from home.

"My heart was in two places — I'm not going to lie," she said.

On the night of Game 4, Hargitay said she shortened her performance so she could make it in time for tip-off.

"I need to be there. I need this for them!" she said. Hargitay sat in the first row next to Taylor Swift and Alana Haim, each of whom wore custom Knicks T-shirts. (Hargitay's said, "Stevie Knicks.")

After the team's improbable 29-point comeback, she was seen on the floor of the Garden with her mouth open, seemingly stunned by what she had just witnessed.

"You're standing in a miracle," Hargitay said. "The world was changed. New York was changed. The bar of what's possible has changed. You can be down 29 points and still win — this is what's in the consciousness of young athletes now."

When a reporter asked Brunson what was next for him after his team won the championship, he said, " Try and get on SVU ." Hargitay confirmed that "it's definitely happening" in a recent interview .

"He's kind of magnificent that way," she said. "He is just open and ready. I don't think there is much Jalen can't do."

Hargitay, who won an Emmy in 2006 for her work on Law & Order: SVU , could win another — while she's hosting the show. Her HBO documentary, My Mom Jayne , has been nominated for three Emmys, including Outstanding Documentary or Nonfiction Special and Outstanding Directing for a Documentary/Nonfiction Program.

The film is about her mother, Jayne Mansfield, who died in a car accident outside New Orleans in 1967. Hargitay and her two older brothers, Zoltán and Miklos, were in the back seat of the vehicle but survived.

In interviews, she has described the documentary as "an archaeological dig" about the generational trauma her family experienced.

"I had no idea how it would be received, so it's been extraordinary to see how it's resonated with people," Hargitay said recently on NBC's Today show . "And that has been the biggest gift of all."

articles.title: Amazon hikes hardware prices by 60%, blaming memory shortage | TechCrunch
articles.summary: As the memory shortage continues to cause trouble for hardware makers, Amazon says it is now being forced to pass on the costs to its consumers.
articles.body:
Over the weekend, Amazon significantly raised the prices of its hardware devices, jacking them up by as much as 60% in some cases.

The price explosion impacted Fire TVs, Echos, Kindles, and Eeros. One egregious example that’s been cited is that of the Echo Dot, one of Amazon’s cheapest smart speakers, the price of which jumped 60% overnight, from $49.99 to $79.99. Price-tracking sites like CamelCamelCamel show the stark uptick, which has previously hovered much lower.

When reached for comment by TechCrunch, Amazon shared the following: “The consumer electronics industry is facing significant increases in memory and storage component costs. After absorbing these increases for as long as we could, we recently adjusted pricing across our product lines.”

The company also said that it would continue to offer occasional promotions to customers over the course of the next year.

Amazon’s price hikes reinforce the reality that it’s a terrible time to buy hardware. The global memory shortage fueled by the AI boom (also known as “ RAMmageddon “) is driving up the cost of producing devices of all stripes. As a result, companies are increasingly passing on the costs to their customers.

In a sign of the times, Apple recently hiked its prices , and has sought to offset the steep new rates by introducing a device-leasing program , thus allowing users to pay off their devices over time.

The RAM shortage is expected to continue throughout 2027 before prices potentially crest and stabilize in 2028.

articles.title: Android is getting its own weird dots to cure car sickness
articles.summary: Google’s Motion Assist taps into your device’s accelerometer and gyroscope to place dots around the periphery of the display that move in harmony with the car.
articles.body: Google is rolling out a new Android feature that’s been proven to reduce, or even eliminate, motion sickness when using a phone inside a moving vehicle. Dubbed Motion Assist by Google, it’s very similar to Apple’s Motion Cues, first introduced in 2024. The Android 17 feature appears to be rolling out in phases, with some Pixel phones getting it first, according to Android Authority. The science behind these magic dots is sound, and addresses the motion sickness felt when staring at a static display while the inner ear feels the car turning, braking, and accelerating. Motion Assist taps into your device’s accelerometer and gyroscope to place dots around the periphery of the display that move in harmony with the motion of the car. When the car turns right, the dots sweep across the screen to the left; when the car brakes, the dots slide forward. [Image: Here’s how it works on Apple devices. I’m here to tell you that this tech really works. As an avid vanlifer, I’m often working on my MacBook and iPhone from the passenger seat while we drive to the next destination. But that’s only possible by activating the anti-nausea feature, otherwise I can’t stomach it. My wife is a convert, too. Google lets you set the opacity of the motion indicators and choose from a variety of shapes and colors. The feature can be configured to turn on automatically when it detects a moving vehicle, or it can be quickly toggled through a tile in your Quick Settings. The feature hasn’t arrived yet on a pair of Pixel devices we tested. But if you’re lucky, you’ll find Motion Assist in your Google Settings under Your Profile and All Services.

articles.summary: Greenworks’ MaximusZ electric riding mower is more than a mower — which it had better be, given the price.
articles.body: The current EV market is flush with variety. I’ve driven single-motor economy-minded machines, dual-motor EVs with all-wheel drive, tri-motor vehicles that dial up the performance stakes, and even wild quad-motor performance cars, like the Rimac Nevera. But this is the first time I’ve ever driven a five-motor EV, one with the agility and speed to turn a 360 even more smoothly than an electric G-Wagon. It also makes quick work of terrible turf. This is, of course, a lawn mower, and it only uses two of those motors to drive the wheels. The other three turn a trio of blades that cut a 54-inch-wide swath in a single pass. It also promises four acres on a charge and is positioned as the ultimate mowing machine. For $8,799, it had better be. For a company that spent much of its life building white-label tools for other brands, Changzhou, China-based Greenworks has quickly leaped to the forefront of battery-powered products for those trying to phase out internal combustion in every facet of their lives. Opening a manufacturing facility in Tennessee in 2023 certainly helped elevate its domestic cred.  The company offers a wide portfolio of products from power tools to go-karts energized by a dizzying array of often incompatible battery technologies. The 80-volt architecture within the MaximusZ mower here is the company’s latest, with Greenworks offering various packs of various sizes. This mower uses four smaller 6.0Ah and two large, 17-pound 16Ah packs to offer a combined battery capacity of 56Ah. That, Greenworks says, is enough to do four acres on a single charge.  [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Charging duties are handled by a disappointingly proprietary charger. I greatly wish Greenworks engineered this thing to work with a standard SAE J1772 plug, or even NACS, but it is quick at least, with Greenworks estimating a full charge at 3.5 hours. At nearly $9,000, the MaximusZ’s cost may seem extreme, but in this space it’s actually competitive. With a maximum speed of 8mph and 41 horsepower on tap, it’s comparable to something like a Stihl RZ 552, which retails for $9,499. It even out-powers some professional-grade machines, like a $18,899 Toro 6000 Series. But is it truly comparable?  It has a few key advantages, the biggest of course being its relative lack of noise and vibration. Not burning gas is an increasingly big deal, too, as is a lack of carburetors to clean and oils to change. Finally, the MaximusZ features a little dumper bed on the back and even a tow hitch.  All those reasons are why I decided to bring one home, but before I could start flaying the fescue, I had to pick a mowing height. That’s easy in the MaximusZ. A pedal on the right lifts the entire mower deck, while a grid defines its height in quarter-inch increments. Step on the pedal, put the pin in the right hole, then take your foot off the pedal, and you’re good to go. It’s almost crude in its simplicity, but it works well.  Next was figuring out the controls. Twist the key and the mower takes about eight seconds to boot up. That’s just long enough to be annoying. Above the key there’s a dim, 4.0-inch LCD that picks up a new scratch every time you look at it too hard. Squint, though, and you can see the current state of charge, maximum mower speed, maximum blade speed, and total runtime.  The buttons under the display let you toggle the blade and mower speeds or enter a menu to change a scant few settings. That 1.5 acres of mowable land I have is split up across a half-dozen small patches, plus a larger pasture, which means I had ample opportunity to test both the MaximusZ’s agility and its stability. I started in the slowest mode until I got the hang of things, which caps you at roughly half the thing’s maximum cutting speed of 8mph. You steer the mower with the two handles. Push them apart from each other, and the mower goes into a sort of park mode. Pull them inward, and the motors are engaged. Each handle controls the corresponding motor on that side, so pushing the right handle all the way forward has the mower turning to the left. Pull the left handle toward you at the same time, and it’ll spin on its own axis. Quite abruptly, if you’re not smooth. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: While I wove and wobbled my way through the first few laps of my pasture, it didn’t take long to get the hang of things. I also quickly realized that the handles weren’t aligned. To go straight ahead, I need to hold the right handle about an inch behind the left. There is, obnoxiously, no way to recalibrate for this, but I eventually got used to it. As I got more confident, I started to dial up the speed, and within a few laps I had the handles pushed all the way forward. I then stepped up from the mower’s slowest setting to the middle, and eventually the fastest.  Mowing at the fastest speed is not the best way to get a perfectly clean cut, but if you, like me, are more interested in getting it done than having it perfect, you can cover a lot of ground quickly.  In smaller areas, that tight turning radius makes for a surprisingly nimble machine, but you do have to be careful about grip. Try to make a too-tight turn, and the MaximusZ tends to light up the inside tire, quickly tearing up the grass and making it look like I was doing donuts out in our pasture.  The biggest challenge, though, is inclines. Officially, the MaximusZ can only be operated at grades of up to 15 degrees. This is a common rating for this type of mower, which many will find limiting. I have succeeded in summiting steeper slopes than that, but grip is the limitation here. With only the rear wheels doing both the driving and the steering for this 767-pound machine, it’s easy to overpower the tires. Running out of grip could mean a crash, and while I imagine it’d take quite a bit to roll this thing over, having a sturdy tubular steel rollover protection structure (ROPS) overhead is definitely reassuring. The MaximusZ has plenty of other niceties, too, like a 2-inch hitch at the front that’s ready for a tow ball, and a smaller hitch at the back with 300-pound towing capacity. The tiny tailgate at the back, though, is its most interesting feature. At 18 inches deep and 28 inches wide, you won’t exactly be hauling a season’s worth of mulch, but 200 pounds of capacity means decent capability. I’ve been using it to haul wood in from the various piles I’ve made over my property from downed trees. There’s even something Greenworks calls an ETO, the electric takeoff, a play on the power takeoff or PTO on most tractors that can drive anything from hay balers to snowblowers. Greenworks only has a few accessories for this so far, but hopefully it will release more in the future. A chipper would be perfect.  All this makes it a surprisingly good utility vehicle, far more practical for day-to-day chore use than the other, competitive mowers. They may cover more ground on a tank of gas, but they’re typically only good for cutting grass.  [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The seat is comfortable and has a built-in, adjustable damper system. That, though, is the only suspension on the machine, making this a rough ride over tree roots and the like. There are integrated USB-A and USB-C ports, a slot for your smartphone, and two cupholders.  And what about noise? I measured 85dB at maximum blade speed, significantly lower than the 90 to 100dB of a commercial-grade mower. That may not sound like much, but a 10dB increase equates to a 10x increase in acoustic force. While you can safely listen to 85dB for eight hours without concern, at 95dB, you can damage your hearing in just 60 minutes. I still wear earplugs to be safe, but I appreciate the relative quiet and lack of harsh vibrations. When the blades are stopped and I’m zipping up and down the driveway, it’s silent and smooth.  At its fastest speed, with the blades on maximum, I can mow my entire property in slightly over one hour. I’ve now done that three times, each time consuming roughly 75 percent of the mower’s battery capacity. Doing the math, that means two acres could be possible at maximum speed. That’s short of the promised four acres, but again, I have a lot of small, oddly shaped patches to mow, and I’m doing it at top speed. Were I mowing at lower speeds, and if I had a single, large pasture, three acres seems like a safe bet without pausing for a recharge or battery swap. That advertised figure of four, though, feels optimistic. The mower has an annoying tendency to drain the four smaller batteries before tapping into the bigger packs. I fear the extra charging cycles these smaller packs face mean they’ll wear out more quickly than if the larger packs were depleted first.  And as far as charging goes, Greenworks’ estimate of 3.5 hours seem fair. Mine has always been done in well less than three.  Again, though, there’s some bad news here. The charger has a loud onboard fan that runs constantly so long as the mower is plugged in, even when fully charged. So I always have to make a point of unplugging the thing after it finishes. While it doesn’t quite deliver on the range, the MaximusZ manages enough capability that I’m not suffering any buyer’s remorse yet. The poor display, the uneven controls, and the unfortunate battery discharge priority are negatives, but none are deal-breakers. The biggest challenge is, of course, the cost. Greenworks markets the MaximusZ as something that not only replaces a high-end zero-turn mower, but also serves as a mini utility vehicle around your property. Its functionality there is limited compared to a full-size UTV vehicle, but given you can easily spend $15,000 on one of those, that helps skew the value equation in this mower’s favor.  My main question now is reliability, but only time will tell whether I’ll need to tap into its four-year warranty. If you’re considering one of these yourself, the best advice I can give is to not pay full price. Greenworks constantly has big discounts. Wait a little while and you’ll save thousands, which might bring the price down to a point where it’s worth the splurge.  Photography by Tim Stevens / The Verge

articles.title: Fitbit founders launch Luffu Link, an LTE health and safety band | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Luffu Link combines all-day health sensing, voice logging, location awareness, and the ability to get help from trusted contacts into a single device, all without needing a phone nearby.
articles.body:
Luffu , a new startup from Fitbit’s co-founders James Park and Eric Friedman, on Tuesday launched Luffu Link, an LTE-enabled health and safety band designed to monitor the wearer’s overall health, both physical and mental. The wearable combines all-day health sensing, voice logging, location awareness, and the ability to get help from trusted contacts into a single device, even when no phone is nearby.

The currently $250 device is available for preorder and is expected to ship in early 2027. It comes in three colors: halo gold, onyx black, and sterling blue.

Luffu Link represents the next step in the startup’s mission to develop an intelligent family care system, as it complements the Luffu health-monitoring app , launched earlier this year. The app uses AI in the background to gather and organize family information, learn day-to-day patterns, and flag notable changes so families can stay aligned and address potential well-being issues.

Luffu was born out of Park and Friedman’s own experiences caring for their families and aging parents. They built Luffu to give families a clearer picture of a loved one’s health without constant check-ins or making them feel monitored.

“When you become a family caregiver, or the CEO of the family, these people are spending an enormous amount of time doing it,” Park said in an interview with TechCrunch. “Research shows over 27 hours a week on average, which is a crazy amount of time…I think technology can play a big role in helping reduce this load, but as we found out, the tools to help them are pretty fragmented,” he said.

Link users can press a button to capture information in the moment by voice, like updates about medications, symptoms, meals, mood, reminders, and more. The Luffu app then organizes that information and incorporates it into the family’s broader context. The company sees its market as including family caregivers, independent older adults, and health- and safety-conscious adults who want to stay on top of their health.

The wearable also continuously collects standard health and wellness data, such as activity, sleep, resting heart rate, calories burned, heart-rate variability (HRV), and breathing rate to identify daily patterns, track changes over time, and provide personalized insights or alerts.

“Link does a lot of what a typical health tracker would do, but it’s not just about tracking,” Park said. “It’s about what Luffu does with that data. It’s looking for patterns, so maybe your activity has been unusually low,” he continues.

“Maybe your sleep patterns have changed. Maybe that change happened after a new medication. So it’s looking at all this data, and it’s not to give families another dashboard full of graphs — I designed a lot of that at Fitbit — it’s to help answer some key questions like ‘what changed? Does it matter? Does somebody need to know?’ And people can just continue to live their life without feeling like they’re being constantly monitored.”

The device uses built-in GPS to keep trusted contacts informed of a wearer’s location, including where they have been and when they enter or leave specific areas. A quick double press also lets the wearer check in with family members without making a call or sending a text. Additionally, built-in LTE lets wearers send a help request without needing to use a phone. (The LTE data service is included so it doesn’t require a separate carrier plan.)

For example, the wearer could press the button and say something like, “I fell and hurt my wrist. Can someone come get me?” Link will then send the voice message along with the wearer’s location, battery level, and health data, like their heart rate and recent activity, to trusted family members.

Unlike other screenless wearables on the market that are focused on individual health and fitness, Link is designed around everyday health and family connection, the company says.

“There’s a trend to have no screens on this new class of wearables, but here, it’s very purposeful,” Park explained. “We want to be in the background. Link is designed to be on your wrist as a quiet guardian throughout your day, and we also wanted to make this feel nothing like a traditional wearable, nothing like a generic-looking fabric brand or a wrist thing with a screen or a bulky pendant that you’re wearing for emergency purposes. So, the device takes a lot of cues from jewelry.”

The startup teased that it’s developing a home device that extends Luffu into the home, marking the next step in its intelligent family care system.

While Link is currently available for preorder at a discounted price, its expected retail price is $300.

articles.title: Apple’s new M6 chip gets more cores and more AI compute
articles.summary: Apple announced new M6 and M5 Ultra chips on Tuesday that will be available in a new Mac Mini and a new Mac Studio, respectively. They’ll be released on September 22nd.
articles.body: Apple has announced a new M6 chip for Macs, along with an M5 Ultra that it says is its “most powerful chip ever,” designed for tasks like 3D rendering and running frontier AI models. The M6 is Apple’s first 2nm chip, which Apple says will bring improvements in performance and power efficiency, and it also has a Dual 16-core Neural Engine for on-device AI workloads. The M6 has a 12-core CPU, up from 10 in the M5, and it includes two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores. (Apple’s “super” core terminology used to refer to performance cores, but it introduced a new type of performance core starting with the M5 Pro and M5 Max.) The company says the CPU offers “the world’s fastest single-threaded performance” and up to 1.2x faster multithreaded performance in comparison to the M5. The chip also has a 12-core GPU, up from 10 cores in the M5, and includes a Neural Accelerator with each core, Apple says. It supports as much as 32GB of unified memory. Apple says that the M5 Ultra uses the company’s UltraFusion interconnect technology to connect two dual-die M5 Max chips together as one quad-die architecture. The M5 Ultra has an up to 36-core CPU with 12 super cores and 24 performance cores, an up to 80-core GPU, and a 32-core Neural Engine. It supports up to 512GB of “high-bandwidth” unified memory, which as usual with the M series isn’t upgradeable after purchase. The M6 chip will be available in a new Mac Mini, while the M5 Ultra will launch in a new Mac Studio. Both computers will be available for preorder beginning Tuesday ahead of a release on September 22nd.

articles.title: Apple launches new Mac Studios with its ‘most powerful chip ever’ — the M5 Ultra
articles.summary: Apple announces new Mac Studio desktops with both M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips. The M5 Ultra is a new processor made from two M5 Max chips, and Apple claims it’s “our most powerful chip ever.”
articles.body: Apple is announcing new models of the Mac Studio, now using the existing M5 Max and a new M5 Ultra. This reunification under one chip generation comes over a year after Apple awkwardly split the Studio between M4 Max and M3 Ultra offerings. (The older-sounding M3 Ultra was actually the more powerful one, and there was never an M4 Ultra chip.) The new Studios look identical to previous generations, utilizing the same small-form-factor chassis since its introduction in 2022 (right down to the USB-A ports on the rear), but inside are Apple’s most powerful SoCs. The new Mac Studio with the existing M5 Max chip comes with 36GB of unified memory and 512GB of storage, starting at $2,499. That matches the current starting price of the M4 Max model after its $500 price hike in June. The new $5,499 M5 Ultra model starts with 96GB of memory and 1TB of storage. That’s only $200 more than the starting price of the outgoing M3 Ultra model, but keep in mind the M3 Ultra launched at a much lower $3,999 last year. These new Studios are set to arrive running macOS 27 Golden Gate on September 22nd, alongside the new Mac Minis. But its highest-end M5 Ultra configuration with a whopping 512GB of memory is coming in late October with pricing TBD for now — though it’s best we start bracing ourselves for the eventual sticker shock. [Image: An M5 Pro / M5 Ultra Mac Studio running DaVinci Resolve Studio and Maxon Redshift on two monitors. These are chip bumps through and through, but what bumps they are. While the RAM and storage amounts for the new Mac Studios match their predecessors, like recent MacBooks, they have storage that’s twice as fast. In its press release, Apple describes the new Studios as “A monumental step for AI” with a claim of up 4.3x faster AI compute in the M5 Ultra. But even when it comes to raw CPU and GPU performance, the M5 Ultra and its up to 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU are said to have up to 1.8x faster graphics and 1.3x faster CPU speed than the M3 Ultra. The memory bandwidth of the M5 Ultra is now up to 1.2TB per second — as if the M3 Ultra’s 819GB per second didn’t sound fast enough. Apple achieved all this in the M5 Ultra by using its next-gen UltraFusion connection to merge two dual-die M5 Max chips together into a quad-die architecture. And it’s why Apple isn’t mincing words by advertising the M5 Ultra as “the most powerful chip ever.” But the Mac Studios also pack another, more pedestrian upgrade for a slight quality-of-life improvement: Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support. With the recent sunsetting of its Mac Pro line of desktops, these Mac Studios are as powerful as Apple computers get. And they’re small enough to fit under your monitor (or up to four of Apple’s 5K / 120Hz Studio Display XDR monitors running at full resolution). But thanks to RAMageddon, Apple’s most powerful chip and its fastest Macs ever are also much pricier than their predecessors were just a short while ago.

articles.title: The lens in Wyze’s new $40 indoor camera retracts for privacy
articles.summary: Wyze’s $40 Indoor Cam Pan can rotate 360 degrees and pan up and down to record 2K videos of moving objects in a room.
articles.body: Wyze announced a new pan-and-tilt security camera today designed for indoor use. The entire Indoor Cam Pan can rotate 360 degrees, while the camera and lens on its front can tilt up and down 103 degrees. When you want privacy, the lens can tilt down until it completely disappears inside the Indoor Cam Pan’s body so it’s unable to see anything happening in your home. The Indoor Cam Pan is available starting today through Wyze’s online store for $39.98. That’s cheaper than Wyze’s $44.98 Cam Pan v3 that’s still available through the company’s website. That older camera can tilt up and down up to 180 degrees and has an IP65 water resistance rating so it can be used outdoors, but it can only record video at 1080p. The new Indoor Cam Pan captures video at a higher 2K resolution, but that’s a slight step down from the more expensive $59.98 Wyze Cam Pan v4 that does 4K. [Image: The camera can be attached to a wall using an optional mount or used standalone and needs access to a power source like a wall outlet. Other features include stealthy operation with what Wyze describes as its “quietest, smoothest motor ever,” as well as AI-powered motion tracking that can ignore objects like robot vacuums while they clean or people and pets not located in customizable detection zones. The camera can keep an eye on things in the dark using night vision and infrared LEDs, but its recording capabilities drop from 20fps to 15fps in low-light conditions. There’s a microSD slot for storing recordings locally on a card up to 512GB in size as well as a speaker and microphone for sounding a 95-decibel alarm or talking to your pets while at work. The Indoor Cam Pan is also compatible with Wyze’s Cam Plus and Cam Unlimited subscription plans that add AI-powered features like alerts that describe what’s been detected.

articles.title: Apple’s new Mac Mini has fresh M6 and M5 Pro chip offerings — and higher prices
articles.summary: Apple’s new Mac Mini for 2026 comes in two versions: one with a new M6 chip and a higher-end model with the existing M5 Pro. It’s the same compact design of the M4 generation but with faster performance and some speedier connections.
articles.body: Apple is announcing a new generation of the Mac Mini, once again offering two models: one with a new M6 chip and a higher-end model with the M5 Pro found in this year’s MacBook Pro. The new Minis have the same tiny design and footprint as the 2024 M4 / M4 Pro models, but with upgraded internals, faster performance, and speedier ethernet ports.  The M6 Mac Mini starts at $899, while the M5 Pro model starts at $1,699. Both cost $100 more than the most recent starting prices of the M4 generation. And while preorders start today, the new Mac Minis won’t ship until September 22nd — hopefully enough time for Apple to stock up on inventory, as the last-gen models became scarce due to higher than expected demand for running AI agents. Like last generation, the new entry-level Mac Mini with an M6 chip starts with 16GB of unified memory and 256GB of storage, and the M5 Pro Mac Mini starts with a 24GB / 512GB configuration. But the storage in all of these models is now twice as fast, just like the recent crop of MacBooks Air and Pro. In addition to the double-speed storage, both M6 and M5 Pro Mac Minis now sport 2.5 gigabit ethernet ports (with the same optional upgrade to 10 gigabit) and they use Apple’s N1 chip for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support. [Image: The Mac Mini is still incredibly small. The M6 Mac Mini now has a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU along with 170GBps of memory bandwidth compared to the M4’s 10-core / 10-core setup and memory bandwidth of 120GBps. Its CPU consists of two super cores (a naming convention that began with the M5 Pro / Max chips), four performance cores, and six efficiency cores — and it’s Apple’s first chip on a 2nm process. Apple claims the M6’s more, faster cores lead to a 40 percent uplift in CPU performance over the M4 generation, and the new 12-core GPU with neural accelerators is up to twice as fast at graphics rendering with ray tracing than the M4 in some games. The M5 Pro of the new Mac Mini is configurable, much like it is on the MacBook Pro: it can be had with up to 18 CPU cores and 20 GPU cores, and it has the same 307GBps of memory bandwidth. Apple claims the Mac Mini with an M5 Pro has significant gains in AI compute and graphics over the outgoing M4 Pro model, thanks in part to the neural accelerator in each GPU core. This should permit heavier AI workloads, including photo and video upscaling, and running larger diffusion models. [Image: Only the ethernet port gets an upgrade in this generation. Some key things haven’t changed on the new Mac Minis — most notably, all the ports besides  the upgraded ethernet. Both Minis maintain two front-facing 10Gbps USB-C ports and the three on the rear of the M6 are faster Thunderbolt 4, while the rear three of the M5 Pro are even speedier Thunderbolt 5 ports. But both the M6 and M5 Pro Mac Minis will ship with macOS 27 Golden Gate preloaded out of the box, offering full compatibility with Apple’s new Siri AI and new Apple Intelligence features. There’s no official launch date for the final public release of macOS 27, but with today’s Mac announcements, it should arrive no later than their September 22nd ship date.

articles.title: Apple’s latest Mac Mini runs on a new M6 chip, and starts at $899
articles.summary: The base model of the Mac Mini comes with 256GB of storage, 16GB of RAM, and costs $899.
articles.body:
Apple on Tuesday unveiled a new Mac Mini that runs on the latest iteration of its “M” processors, the M6.

The base model of this device comes with 256GB of storage, 16GB of RAM, and costs $899. It’s available for preorder now, but the device will ship only after September 22, the company said.

Apple said the new Mac Mini’s AI performance is 4x better than the M4 model, and storage and graphics are twice as fast. The new processor has a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, as compared to the 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU on the M4.

Alongside the M6 model, there is also a Mac Mini with the M5 Pro chip. This model comes with base storage of 512GB and RAM of 24GB, and starts at $1,699. By default the M5 Pro chip ships with a 15-core CPU and 16-core GPU, and can be upgraded to a 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU.

Both variants have Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, along with a 2.5GB Ethernet port. Users can upgrade to a 10GB port as well.

The new Mac Minis will start shipping on September 22 with macOS 27 and Siri AI.

The Mac Minis have grown popular over the past year among tech enthusiasts for running local AI agents such as OpenClaw and Hermes. People were selling Mac Minis at marked-up prices on platforms like eBay earlier this year due to rising demand.

Besides the new Mac Minis, the company also released new Mac Studio models that run on the M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips, starting at $2,499 and $5,499, respectively. The M5 Max base model comes with 36GB of unified memory and 512GB of storage. The M5 Ultra base model has 96GB of unified memory and 1TB storage.

Earlier this year, the company discontinued the previous base model of the Mac Mini, which offered 256GB of storage and retailed for $599. It was until now offering the 512GB version with an M4 processor for $799 as the base model.

articles.title: Tesla Cybertruck is now a more expensive sales dud.
articles.summary:
The low-volume truck that Elon Musk once claimed would sell over 250,000 units annually is now about $5,000 more expensive, according to Reuters. Two trims are going up in price: the dual-motor version is now $74,990, up from $69,990; and the all-wheel drive Cybertruck is $84,990, up from $79,990. Tesla has futzed with the truck’s lineup before, introducing a $60,000 all-wheel drive version and jacking up the Cyberbeast trim by $15,000. But it’s done little to juice sales, with only 3,519 Cybertrucks delivered in Q1 2026, down 45 percent year over year.
